title: Decision Auditor: matrix metrics and sample capture for region/tier/fallback routing
creator: Marisol Vega
body:
Summary:
We need a focused observability feature that captures a compact decision matrix and representative sampled artifacts for each routing decision made at region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variant selection. The goal is to make post-hoc RCA and live debugging faster and cheaper by: 1) emitting a small decision matrix per request with reason codes, latencies, and cost deltas; 2) attaching a bounded set of sampled artifacts (headers, short traces, token counts, model variant identifiers, sampling seed) for failed or high-cost requests; 3) surfacing aggregated histograms and pivot tables in Console for team-friendly debugging.

Problem context and motivation:
- Current routing telemetry emits verbose per-hop logs and large payload attachments for many requests, increasing storage and query costs.
- When region/tier/fallback routing is involved, SREs and Platform Engineers spend hours correlating traces, logs, and console dashboards to understand why a request fell back or crossed tiers.
- We lack a compact, machine-friendly decision artifact that can be searched and joined to traces and cost reports without pulling full request payloads.

Proposed approach:
1) Decision Matrix: emit a JSON-serializable flat record per request (max 1KB) with fields: request_id, chosen_region, chosen_tier, chosen_model_variant, decision_reasons (compressed codes), decision_latency_ms, estimated_token_cost_delta, sampling_bucket, and provenance_version. The record is intended for fast index and join against tracing events.
2) Representative Sample Capture: for requests that meet sampling rules (errors, SLO breaches, rare fallback paths, and ~0.1% baseline), attach a small artifact bundle that includes anonymized prompt fingerprint, 1-2 sample tokens of input, the sampled KV cache size, and a short breadcrumb trace of routing decisions across hops (max 3 hops). These bundles are stored in a low-retention blob store with index pointers in the decision matrix.
3) Aggregations and Console Views: produce daily histograms per region/tier/model_variant for decision_latency_ms, fallback_rate, and estimated_cost_delta. Add pivot controls in Console to filter by decision_reasons and sampling_bucket.
4) Backwards-compatible instrumentation: decision matrix emission should be gated behind a feature flag and default to reduced schema for hosted customers. Private/Dedicated deployments can enable extended fields.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Size vs fidelity: keep the matrix compact to avoid the high cardinality log problem. Use short enumerated reason codes and store long textual rationale only in sampled bundles.
- Privacy: sampled bundles must be scrubbed and never contain PII. Work with Trust & Safety to finalize scrubbing rules.
- Queryability: store matrix records in our clickhouse cluster (or Postgres for low-volume tenants) with TTL-based rollups to support fast queries.
- Cost: low-retention of sampled bundles (30 days) and compact matrices should keep incremental cost below 5% of current telemetry spend.

Success metrics:
- Mean time to identify root cause for routing fallback incidents reduced from 4 hours to <1 hour for target incidents.
- Query response time for routing decision lookups under 200ms.
- Fallback investigation events that require pulling full request payloads reduced by 80%.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Final enumeration of decision reasons and canonical codes (see design doc).
- Exact sampling rates for baseline vs. error vs. rare-path buckets.
- Where sampled bundles should be stored (S3 vs internal blob store) and retention length.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/routing-decision-matrix (draft)
- Dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/decision-auditor-mockups
- Related infra work: ENG-87211 (decision router schema), ENG-84400 (telemetry storage indexing)

Notes for rollout:
Phase 1 (feature-flagged): emit minimal decision matrix and low-rate sampling (errors + 0.01% baseline) to production for 2 weeks. Validate storage and query performance.
Phase 2: enable aggregated histograms and Console pivots for internal users. Increase baseline sampling to 0.1% if stability holds.
Phase 3: public opt-in for Hosted API and default enabled for Dedicated/Private with extended schema options.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision matrix emitted for 100% of routed requests when feature flag is on and successfully indexed within telemetry cluster.
- Sampled bundles created and retrievable by pointer in decision matrix for sampled requests.
- Console shows new pivot controls and histogram panels for region/tier/model_variant within release runtime-1.22.
- Security review completed for sample scrubbing rules and storage retention.
- Query performance: decision lookup queries return in <200ms for 95th percentile.
tasks: Define reason code enum and update decision router to emit codes
Implement compact decision matrix serializer and emission path
Add sample bundle generator with scrubbing pipeline
Wire indexer to store matrix records in telemetry cluster with TTL
Create Console UI pivots and histogram panels (internal-only in Phase 1)
Run canary traffic and validate storage/cost/latency targets
comments: 2026-03-06 - Jonah Park: Spiked a serializer that produces 850 bytes for a typical matrix record. Memory and CPU overhead look acceptable in canary. See spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/decision-router/pull/178
2026-03-08 - Marisol Vega: Design review held with SRE and Privacy. Need to add scrubbing step for IP-like tokens and named entities before storing samples.
2026-03-09 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Agreed to store matrices in clickhouse with 7d raw TTL and 60d aggregated rollup. Added ENG-87211 as dependency for schema migration.
2026-03-11 - Jonah Park: Canary started on region-us-east-1, sampling errors + 0.01% baseline. Initial dashboards show decision_latency_ms median at 12ms. No obvious cost spike.
2026-03-13 - QA (Anika Bose): Found edge case when fallback chain length >3; sampler truncated hops incorrectly. Added follow-up task to preserve hop endpoint IDs even when truncating payloads.
2026-03-14 - Jonah Park: Security review requested. Opening checklist for scrubbing rules and retention policy: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/routing-scrub-checklist
